acceptance_criteria.criterion: The dashboard renders a visible filter toolbar between the page header and the project list.
The toolbar contains a search input with placeholder "Search projects…" and type="search".
The toolbar contains a repository filter <select> with an "All repositories" default option and one option per registered repository (value = repo ID, label = repo Name).
The toolbar contains a sort selector <select> with "Alphabetical" (value alpha, default) and "Last Activity" (value activity) options.
If api.repositories.list() fails, the toolbar still renders with search and sort controls (no repository dropdown), and a toast error message is shown.
The toolbar's CSS layout follows the flex pattern established by .error-log-filter-bar.
DOM clearing uses clearElement() from utils/dom.js — no innerHTML = '' for container clearing.
All three controls fire an onFilterChange() callback with the current filter/sort state when their values change. The search input uses a debounced input event (~250ms).

summary: Implemented the filter/sort toolbar UI component for the dashboard project list. Changes include: (1) Added debounce() helper in dashboard.js. (2) Added buildFilterToolbar() async function that builds a .project-filter-toolbar div with: a search input (type=search, placeholder='Search projects…', debounced 250ms input event), an optional repository filter <select> populated from api.repositories.list() with 'All repositories' default option (omitted on API failure with toast shown), and a sort <select> with Alphabetical (alpha, default) and Last Activity (activity) options. All three controls invoke onFilterChange() with the current FilterState. (3) Updated renderDashboard() to declare listContainer first, build the toolbar asynchronously with buildFilterToolbar(), then insert toolbar → listContainer → createSection into the container (toolbar sits between page header and project list). (4) Added .project-filter-toolbar CSS to styles.css using the same flex layout pattern as .error-log-filter-bar. All 100 existing GUI tests continue to pass.

comments.note: dashboard.js/showLoading(): uses innerHTML to set a loading spinner string. This is consistent with how it was before my changes (pre-existing pattern), but diverges from the clearElement() approach used for container clearing. A future improvement could replace this with DOM API calls to stay consistent. Not in scope of this WP.

dashboard.js: The JSDoc @type import reference in renderDashboard() uses `import('./dashboard.js').FilterState` — a self-referential import type. It works for tooling hints but is slightly unusual. A module-level @typedef export would be cleaner. Low priority, does not affect runtime behaviour.

dashboard.js/buildFilterToolbar(): The toolbar currently has no visible labels (e.g., 'Filter by:') for sighted users scanning the page. The error-log-filter-bar uses .filter-label elements. ARIA labels are present for screen readers, but visual labels could improve discoverability. Consider adding visible labels in a follow-up pass if UX review surfaces the issue.

summary: All 8 acceptance criteria verified against the implementation. All 100 existing GUI tests pass with no regressions. The toolbar component is correctly structured and follows established conventions.

comments.note: buildFilterToolbar(): If api.repositories.list() returns a non-empty array where some repos have missing id/name fields, those options get empty string values. Selecting such an option would behave identically to 'All repositories' (repoId: ''). This is safe degradation but could cause subtle confusion. A future improvement could filter out repos with no usable ID.

debounce(): clearTimeout(undefined) on first invocation is a no-op — safe. The closure captures searchInput.value at call time (inside the debounced callback), which is correct and avoids stale value reads.

buildFilterToolbar(): The repo dropdown is entirely omitted when repos.length === 0 (successful empty fetch). This means if a user has no repos registered, there is no repo filter at all — which is logically correct but worth noting for future UX consideration (e.g., disabled placeholder dropdown).

The filterState object in renderDashboard() is maintained correctly and passed to both buildFilterToolbar() and the onFilterChange handler.
